value.rationale: Fingerprinter identified this as a Definitions/Glossary sheet.
The sheet has "PRODUCT FRAMEWORK ID" refIds like "CORE.PRD.001"/"CORE.LOB.001"/"CORE.COV.001" alongside PRODUCT, LINE OF BUSINESS, COVERAGE, and SUB-COVERAGE columns forming the product hierarchy.

Columns "FORM NAME", "FORM NUMBER" (e.g. "AC 001 AZ"), "FORM EDITION DATE", "FORM CATEGORY", and "DYNAMIC DATA" with values like "State Endorsement – Arizona" identify this as a form specification/attachment schedule sheet.

The sheet is titled "Core Forms Dynamic Data" and lists form numbers like "AC 107" with form names such as "Waiver of Subrogation Endorsement" alongside dynamic field metadata ("Reporting Period Ending Date"), which is a classic forms Dynamic Data schedule.
The sheet has "RULE ID" (e.g. "CORE.RU001"), "RULE CATEGORY", "RULE CONDITION" and "RULE OUTCOME" columns rather than calculation/algorithm-step columns, marking it as a governance rules sheet.

Despite the name "Rule References", the stacked tables contain factor/lookup content like "TABLE NAME: Minimum Premiums" with "Amount ($)" values keyed by class ("Truck/Jeep/SUV", "Camper Trailer") and state applicability lists, which is an actuarial factor/rate table rather than condition->outcome rules.

The sheet has "RATING STEP ID" (e.g. "CORE.RAT.0001.01"), "ALGORITHM STEP" ("Base rate", "Model year factor"), "CALCULATION", and "RATE REFERENCE" columns, making it a Core-format rating algorithm sheet.
